links.reason: Hebrews repeats that on the seventh day “God rested from all His works”; Genesis tells how God finished and rested from “all His work.”
Hebrews says whoever enters God’s rest rests from work, “just as God did”; Genesis says God rested on the seventh day.
Hebrews calls land that produces “thorns and thistles” worthless; Genesis says “thorns and thistles” will be yielded to you.
Hebrews repeats “because God had taken him away” about Enoch, who in Genesis walked with God and then was no more.
Hebrews says Melchizedek met Abraham “returning from the slaughter of the kings”; Genesis tells of that return, when the king of Sodom met him.
Hebrews repeats what God had said to Abraham in Genesis: “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
Hebrews says God had no one greater, so He “swore by Himself”; in Genesis, the LORD says, “By Myself I have sworn.”
Hebrews repeats the promise “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants”; Genesis adds “like the stars in the sky.”
Hebrews says descendants came as numerous as “the stars in the sky” and “the sand on the seashore”; Genesis has the same words.
Hebrews says Jacob “worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff”; Genesis says Israel “bowed in worship at the head of his bed.”
Hebrews says “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned”; Exodus says “whether man or beast, he must not live.”
Hebrews repeats “This is the blood of the covenant,” the words Moses says in Exodus as he splatters the blood on the people.
Hebrews repeats “according to the pattern shown you on the mountain” as a warning to Moses; Exodus has the same command.
Hebrews says hope “enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain”; Leviticus says to take the censer and incense “inside the veil.”
Hebrews says the bodies of animals “are burned outside the camp”; Leviticus says the bull and the goat “must be taken outside the camp.”
Hebrews says “Moses was faithful in all God’s house”; Numbers says of “My servant Moses,” “he is faithful in all My house.”
Hebrews says “Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house”; Numbers has “he is faithful in all My house.”
Hebrews repeats “our God is a consuming fire”; Deuteronomy says “the LORD your God is a consuming fire.”
Hebrews says Moses said, “I am trembling with fear”; in Deuteronomy 9:19 the speaker says, “I was afraid of the anger and wrath.”
Hebrews repeats Deuteronomy’s rule: death “on the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
Hebrews warns that no “root of bitterness” should spring up; Deuteronomy warns that no “root among you” should bear “poisonous and bitter fruit.”
Hebrews says God said, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you”; Deuteronomy says the LORD “will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Hebrews repeats “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay” from Deuteronomy 32:35.
Hebrews says “The Lord will judge His people”; Deuteronomy 32:36 says “the LORD will vindicate His people.”
Hebrews repeats “Let all God’s angels worship Him”; the same words stand in Deuteronomy.
Hebrews says God said, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you”; Joshua says “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Hebrews repeats “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son”; 2 Samuel has nearly the same words.
Hebrews says “I will put My trust in Him”; 2 Samuel says “My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge.”
Hebrews asks whether God ever said to an angel, “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father,” the words found in Psalms.
Hebrews says the One who spoke to Christ said, “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father,” as in Psalms.
Hebrews repeats the question “What is man that You are mindful of him,” which Psalms also asks.
Hebrews repeats “You made him a little lower than the angels,” as Psalms says, and “You crowned him with glory and honor.”
Hebrews repeats “placed everything under his feet”; Psalms has the same words.
Hebrews repeats “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers”; Psalms 22:22 has the same words, ending “in the assembly.”
Hebrews repeats “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire” and has “a body You prepared for Me” where Psalms has “my ears You have opened.”
Hebrews repeats “burnt offerings and sin offerings”; Psalms 40:6 says “You did not require,” where Hebrews says “You took no delight.”
Hebrews repeats “Then I said” and “it is written about Me in the scroll”; Psalms 40:7 has the same words with “me.”
Hebrews says “I have come to do Your will, O God”; Psalms 40:8 says “I delight to do Your will, O my God.”
Hebrews repeats “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever” and “justice is the scepter of Your kingdom”; Psalms 45:6 has the same words.
Hebrews repeats “You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness”; Psalms 45:7 has the same words and goes on “with the oil of joy.”
Hebrews repeats the call in Psalms, “Today, if you hear His voice”, and the warning about fathers who tested Him in the wilderness.
Hebrews repeats the call in Psalms: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts”.
Hebrews says God spoke through David and repeats the words of Psalms: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts”.
Hebrews repeats “do not harden your hearts” from Psalms, but writes “the rebellion” where Psalms names Meribah and Massah.
Hebrews repeats “do not harden your hearts” from Psalms, with “the rebellion” where Psalms names Meribah.
Hebrews repeats “do not harden your hearts” from Psalms, which ties the words to “the day at Massah in the wilderness”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms: “where your fathers tested and tried Me”; Psalms adds “though they had seen My work”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms: God says “I was angry with that generation” and the people “have not known My ways”.
Hebrews repeats the oath in Psalms: “They shall never enter My rest”.
Hebrews asks to whom God swore that they would “never enter His rest”; Psalms gives the oath: “They shall never enter My rest”.
Hebrews repeats the oath in Psalms, “They shall never enter My rest”, and says those who believed do enter that rest.
Hebrews repeats “They shall never enter My rest”, a saying that Psalms gives as an oath.
Hebrews speaks of whoever “enters God’s rest”; Psalms records an oath: “They shall never enter My rest”.
Hebrews has “Let all God’s angels worship Him”; Psalms says “Worship Him, all you gods!”
Hebrews repeats Psalms: “You laid the foundations of the earth”, and “the heavens are the work of Your hands”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms: “They will perish, but You remain”; they “will all wear out like a garment”.
Hebrews repeats the words of Psalms: “You remain the same, and Your years will never end”.
Hebrews says He makes His angels winds and His servants “flames of fire”; Psalms says He makes the winds His messengers.
Hebrews says the Son “sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms in a question about the angels: “Sit at My right hand” and “a footstool for Your feet”.
Hebrews says a high priest “sat down at the right hand of the throne”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Hebrews says the Priest “sat down at the right hand of God”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms, changing “Your feet” to “His feet”: He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool.
Hebrews says Jesus “sat down at the right hand of the throne of God”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek”.
Hebrews repeats Psalms as testimony: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek”.
Hebrews says Jesus became a priest with an oath and repeats Psalms: “will not change His mind”.
Hebrews repeats “I will not be afraid” and “What can man do to me” from Psalms, but says the Lord is “my helper”.
Hebrews repeats Proverbs: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord”; Proverbs has “do not reject the discipline of the LORD”.
Hebrews repeats Proverbs: “the Lord disciplines the one He loves”.
Hebrews says “Make straight paths for your feet”; Proverbs says “Make a level path for your feet”.
Hebrews repeats Isaiah: “I will put My trust in Him”; in Isaiah, the speaker also says “I will wait for the LORD”.
Hebrews repeats Isaiah: “Here am I, and the children”, then “God has given Me” where Isaiah says “the LORD has given me”.
Hebrews speaks of “raging fire that will consume all adversaries”; Isaiah says “The fire set for Your enemies will consume them”.
Hebrews says “In just a little while” He who is coming will come; Isaiah says “Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed”.
Hebrews says “strengthen your limp hands and weak knees”; Isaiah says “Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees”.
Hebrews says He helps “the descendants of Abraham”; Isaiah says to Israel, “descendant of Abraham My friend”.
Hebrews says He helps “the descendants of Abraham”; Isaiah says “I have chosen and not rejected you”.
Hebrews says Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; Isaiah says “He bore the sin of many.”
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s words about “a new covenant with the house of Israel” and a longer promise that follows.
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s words “not be like the covenant I made with their fathers” when the LORD took them by the hand.
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s promise “I will be their God, and they will be My people,” with laws put in minds and written on hearts.
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s “the covenant I will make with” and “after those days,” and swaps the order of hearts and minds.
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah: no one will “teach his neighbor or his brother,” because “they will all know Me.”
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s promise “I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”
Hebrews repeats Jeremiah’s promise to “remember” sins “no more,” and adds “lawless acts” to the sins.
Hebrews repeats Habakkuk’s words “and will not delay,” saying One “who is coming” where Habakkuk says a vision “will surely come.”
Hebrews repeats Habakkuk’s words “will live by faith,” saying “My righteous one” where Habakkuk says “the righteous.”
Hebrews repeats Haggai’s words “Once more” and “I will shake,” saying the earth and heaven; Haggai says “the heavens and the earth.”
Hebrews repeats Psalms: “So I swore on oath in My anger”, and the people “shall never enter My rest”.
Hebrews repeats “They shall never enter My rest”, a saying that Psalms gives after “Today, if you hear His voice”.
Hebrews repeats “in the order of Melchizedek” from Psalms, saying God designated him as high priest.
Hebrews repeats “the covenant I will make with” and “after those days” from Jeremiah’s promise of a new covenant.
Hebrews says Moses “took the blood of calves and goats” and sprinkled the people; Exodus says Moses “took the blood, splattered it on the people.”
Hebrews says “burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire”; Psalms says “Burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not require”.
Hebrews says God said, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you”; Deuteronomy says “He will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Hebrews says “I will not be afraid”; Psalms says “The LORD is my light and my salvation” and asks whom to fear.
